purpose: Play Level 1 of the reconstructed Abuse (1996) through the five-operation player interface, choosing one legal action per decision, and compare that play fairly with a scripted search baseline and a random floor.
prohibited_actions: change game state except through step() with an action from legal_actions()
read the World object, level files, the original Lisp or C, or docs/rule-source-map.md
use the evaluator's progress measure or route
access credentials or the runner's environment
retry a failed model request, repair an answer, or substitute a fixture for a live player
memory_policy: Set per experiment condition, and nothing persists across episodes. M0: the current observation only. M1: plus the last 8 turns (action, result, health, position, events). M2: plus the model's own notes (at most 600 characters) and an automap summary built only from past observations.
context_sources: src/abuse_remake/agent/observation.py:build_observation (the 316x162 view, HUD, on-screen tiles, objects and events)
src/abuse_remake/agent/prompts.py:SYSTEM (manual-level knowledge and the baseline's priors, no map knowledge)

model_choice.default_mode: offline: the random and scripted players; the model player runs only when asked for, and in abuse-eval only with --live
model_choice.live_model: Explicit COURSE_MODEL (or --model) for the chosen provider; no model ID is in the code. The model the API reports (Vertex model_version, Anthropic and OpenAI model) is recorded per decision in traces and listed in reports.

prompts_or_system_instructions: src/abuse_remake/agent/prompts.py: SYSTEM, NOTES_RULE, REPLY_RULE, system_prompt(), decision_schema(), render_turn()
named_failure_modes: illegal action (not in legal_actions): refused and counted
an answer that is not a JSON object, or an action that is not a string: refused and counted
provider timeout, rate limit, connection or server error: a refused decision with its category
truncated answer (output cap, including thinking tokens) or a continuation: refused as truncated
rejected or missing credentials: fatal, the episode ends as 'player failed'
late reply after the decision timeout: dropped by request id, its tokens still counted
repeating an action that does not move the player: visible in M1/M2 history; not prevented
evaluation_cases: Offline and in CI: tests/test_player_interface.py, tests/test_model_player.py (mocked provider clients, real SDK error types), tests/test_evaluate.py (an eval smoke run, budget caps, statistics, the tuning/report split) and tests/test_evidence.py (every committed trace replays). Live: the suite declared in SUITE.md before any tuning, eval/configs/midterm.toml (reported) and eval/configs/midterm-tuning.toml (tuning only), after eval/configs/live-smoke.toml, through abuse-eval --live once the owner approves the estimate.
logging_policy: Each decision's trace row (runs/<run>/traces/<player>/<scenario>-s<seed>.jsonl) records the tick, the action, whether it was accepted, the episode's and the player's errors, the raw reply (truncated to 600 characters), the note, the M2 notes, the usage (model, tokens, latency, error category) and a hash of the observation. Prompts are not stored: they are a pure function of the observation, which --full-obs stores. No credentials or environment are logged.
human_override_points: choose the provider, the model (COURSE_MODEL) and the memory condition
approve the token and cost estimate before any live run
stop a run at any time (results are written as episodes finish)
merge each PR and submit the course PR
native_artifact: src/abuse_remake/agent/players/model_player.py: a player program speaking the JSON-lines protocol in src/abuse_remake/agent/protocol.py, with structured output validated by the episode
fallback: A failed request is a refused decision: counted, fed back in last_result, never retried, repaired or replaced by a fixture. A fatal credential error ends the episode as 'player failed'. Live players are reported as 'not run' when --live is not given or the run's token cap is reached.
limitations: Process isolation limits what the runner hands a player; it is not a security sandbox against a hostile program.
The token budgets rely on the usage the player process reports from the provider's response.
The scripted baseline is deterministic in practice, so intervals over seeds can have zero width; they measure seed variation, not other ways a player could play.
Comparisons are between fixed players under equal budgets. Self-play alone does not establish learning or strong play; human playtests give the human reference.
Level 1 only. Death ends an episode, a design choice (harness); the original reloads the last save.
The live comparison needs the owner's Vertex AI setup and has not been run at the time of writing.

agent_team.purpose: Build the reconstruction, the player interface, the players and the evaluation under the student's direction.
agent_team.tools_and_permissions: Repository read and write, tests, git on feature branches, opening PRs; no merges, no tags, no credential access without asking.
agent_team.outputs: Feature branches, passing tests, map rows and a change summary per PR.
agent_team.handoff: The PR and its summary go to the independent reviewer; findings and fixes are recorded in docs/reviews/PR-<n>.md.
agent_team.human_approval: The student merges every PR and submits the course PR.

agent_team.purpose: One procedure for porting or changing a rule: cite the original at its pinned commit, add the map row, write the failing test, port with the original arithmetic, check the player boundary, summarise.
agent_team.tools_and_permissions: Runs inside the implementation agent with its permissions.
agent_team.outputs: A map row, a test, the port and a summary.
agent_team.handoff: The summary is the reviewer's input.
agent_team.human_approval: The student accepts or rejects the summary's assumptions.

agent_team.purpose: One procedure for a fair repeated comparison: commit the config, estimate, get approval, smoke-test, run, report every episode, keep the evidence.
agent_team.tools_and_permissions: Runs inside the implementation agent; live runs only after the student approves the estimate.
agent_team.outputs: A run directory, a report and selected traces under evidence/.
agent_team.handoff: The report goes to the student.
agent_team.human_approval: The student approves every live run's cost and the report's conclusions.

agent_team.purpose: Check evidence, fidelity to the cited original, agreement of engine, test and map, test strength, the player's boundary and fair evaluation.
context: the change summary and diff, read through git objects
agent_team.tools_and_permissions: Read-only (Read, Grep, Glob, read-only git); a fresh context that did not write the change; no network or model calls.
agent_team.outputs: Findings as [blocking | should fix | note] file:line lines, or 'No findings'.
agent_team.handoff: Findings go to the student and the implementation agent; fixes and decisions are recorded in docs/reviews/PR-<n>.md.
agent_team.human_approval: The student decides every finding; the reviewer cannot approve or merge.

playing_agent_interface.sees: the JSON results of observe(), legal_actions() and step() only, sent over the JSON-lines protocol to a separate process with a minimal environment
never_sees: the World object or any engine object
level files, the original Lisp or C, or docs/rule-source-map.md
enemy health, AI state, links, timers or the random table
credentials (only the model player process gets its provider's SDK variables, which never enter prompts or traces)
playing_agent_interface.runner_constraint: The runner (agent/runner.py, agent/evaluate.py, game/spectate.py) holds the AbuseEpisode; players run as child processes and receive only JSON. Tests check the observation contents, the copies, the environment and the end message.
